alignments.note: Subject pronoun and auxiliary are helpers on the passive verb; head on the lexical participle (rules 7, 9, 17).
Supplied antecedent pronoun is a helper on the relative (rule 7); head on the relativizer.
Greek anarthrous, so the supplied determiner is an ordinary helper on the noun (rule 51).
Modal and copula are helpers on the passive verb; head on the lexical verb (rules 7, 9, 17).
The ASV gives the noun no determiner, so the article carries nothing and the case preposition stays with the noun (rules 21, 23).
Case preposition rides with the noun where no determiner is written (rule 21).
The particle 'away' belongs to the verb's own English idiom for ἐκπίπτω; head on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17).
